document.description: BcoG is a beta-keto acid cleavage enzyme of Sinorhizobium meliloti that converts 3-dehydrocarnitine and acetyl-CoA to betainyl-CoA and acetoacetate. This reaction connects the carnitine-dehydrogenase and betainyl-CoA-hydrolase activities of the fused BcoE-BcoF protein. Purified-enzyme chemistry was measured with the 3D0a2 protein, whose sequence matches the strain 1021 reference through Rm2011. Native GBB utilization differs between strains, so this catalytic identity does not establish growth of strain 1021 on GBB.

document.description: BcoE-BcoF is a fused dehydrogenase–thioesterase of Sinorhizobium meliloti carnitine metabolism. Its N-terminal region oxidizes L-carnitine to 3-dehydrocarnitine with NAD+, and its C-terminal hotdog region hydrolyzes betainyl-CoA to glycine betaine and CoA. The same protein also hydrolyzes carnitinyl-CoA, releasing carnitine during upstream gamma-butyrobetaine utilization. These three activities were measured on the sequence-matched 3D0a2 protein. The fusion supplies two distinct catalytic roles in carnitine degradation, with BcoG performing the intervening cleavage reaction. Native GBB-growth phenotypes differ between Rm2011 and strain 1021 despite identical local coding sequences.

document.description: PP_0303 is a 294-residue CdhC-type beta-keto acid cleavage enzyme in the Pseudomonas putida KT2440 carnitine catabolic locus. Its sequence is approximately 82% identical to P. aeruginosa CdhC, and its placement beside LcdH and the CdhB-type thioesterase supports a role converting 3-dehydrocarnitine and acetyl-CoA into betainyl-CoA and acetoacetate. The target protein occurs in a published enzyme screen with dehydrocarnitine and additional substrates; its complete substrate-specific kinetic profile and physiological alternatives remain unresolved.

review.summary: Target-specific screening signals prevent rejection, but the KAH positive-call threshold is unresolved.
review.reason: PMID:24240508 Dataset 2 maps Q88R31 (KT2440 PP_0303) to BKACE_511; Dataset 4 includes BKACE511 with dehydrocarnitine screening values 146.407/237.1 and (S)-KAH values 50.55/81.021. These are pre-process screen values, not target kinetic constants. The supplemental statistical description requires a substrate-specific cutoff, which was not recovered from accessible main text. Thus the previous categorical wrong-substrate interpretation is unwarranted, but a confirmed KAH activity or native lysine-degradation role cannot be asserted from these values alone. Keep UNDECIDED pending the processed KAH call or complete assay analysis; the carnitine role has independent conserved-locus, target-screen and characterized-ortholog support.
